subject: Discovery recap — MedGrowth: technical fit & PoC plan
thread_messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medgrowth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — MedGrowth: technical fit & PoC plan

Alex — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- High false positives in clinical triage pipeline; model hallucinations are impacting workflow efficiency.
- Current infra struggles with concurrent inference during peak clinic hours (latency spikes).
- Data residency and logs/audit visibility required for upcoming vendor assessment.

Goals you described
- Replace current retrieval + LLM pipeline with a production-grade inference stack that reduces median latency and hallucinations for triage summaries.
- Baseline SLO: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for 512-token requests under expected concurrency.
- Safe rollout: canary to a subset of clinics and audit logs for each request.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Inference: self-hosted LLMs (Bison-v2 derivative) behind a Go microservice
- Orchestration: Kubernetes in AWS us-west-2; RDS for metadata
- Auth: Okta SSO, internal keys, SOC2 gap assessment in progress

Success criteria for a 2-week PoC
- Functional: Redwood integrates with existing API/ingestion with <2 integration days for devs.
- Performance: demonstrated 95th percentile latency < 300ms for 512-token baseline during a defined load test.
- Quality: reduction in triage hallucination rate by >=20% on a shared prompt set.
- Controls: request-level audit logs delivered to your S3 bucket and access patterns enabled for compliance review.

Proposed PoC scope & timeline (tentative)
- Week 0 (May 10): Kickoff, exchange test prompts, grant sandbox API keys, share benchmark harness.
- Week 1 (May 11–17): Integration, basic traffic ramp, Python/Node SDK verification.
- Week 2 (May 18–24): Load tests, quality evals, collect telemetry and handoff results.

Owners
- Redwood: Ben Carter (sales/technical lead), Marissa Cole (CS/onsite support), Vivek Kulkarni (solutions engineer)
- MedGrowth: Alex Johnson (PM), Jordan Lee (CTO)

Immediate asks from us
1) Can you confirm the PoC dates above (May 10–24) and owners?
2) Please share the sample prompt set and one representative anonymized record we can use for quality checks (S3 or Drive link).
3) Any hard constraints for data residency (must stay in your VPC / specific S3 bucket)?

Attachments: I attached a short draft SOW and a high-level infra diagram for reference.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medgrowth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medgrowth.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — MedGrowth: technical fit & PoC plan

Ben — thanks for the thorough write-up, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and responses below.

Clarifications / constraints
- Data residency: For the PoC we can provide a sandbox S3 bucket in our AWS account (us-west-2). Production will require VPC peering or Private Deployment; we'll flag that for contract discussions.
- SDK preference: our infra team prefers Python first (main triage service is in Python), Node optional for a lightweight ingestion service.
- Audit/logs: we need request-level logs retained for 90 days in a write-once bucket for compliance review.

Success metrics: we agree with the criteria but would add a cost target — we'd like to understand estimated $/100k tokens on your hosted path vs Dedicated. Not a hard blocker for PoC but important for ROI.

Sample data: attaching a sanitized sample record and the stack summary (attached). We'll drop the full prompt set into the shared Drive link once we confirm the kickoff.

PoC dates: May 10–24 work for us. Jordan will lead the infra work and will be copied on implementation threads; procurement will follow up on contract items during/after the PoC.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product — MedGrowth
alex.johnson@medgrowth.ai | +1 (206) 555-0112

Attachments: medgrowth-current-stack-summary.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medgrowth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — MedGrowth: technical fit & PoC plan

Alex — perfect, thanks for the confirmations. A few concrete next items from Redwood: 

Immediate deliverables (from Redwood)
- SOW draft (attached) with PoC scope and acceptance criteria — Ben to deliver by EOD Mon (May 3).
- Sandbox keys & a test harness (we'll provide a small load test harness and a script to replay your sample payloads).
- Cost estimate for the two paths you asked about (hosted vs Dedicated) — preliminary numbers by May 6.

Integration notes
- SDKs: we'll prioritize the Python SDK path for the PoC; Node SDK verification is optional in Week 1.
- API compatibility: Redwood can present an OpenAI-style REST endpoint; we can also optionally provide a gRPC endpoint later if Jordan prefers lower-latency RPC.
- Authn: we'll support temporary API keys for PoC; for production we'll work with your Okta team on service accounts.

Proposed log delivery for audit: Redwood can stream request logs to your S3 bucket in ndjson format with request_id/trace_id and model metadata — we'll ensure 90-day retention is achievable. 

Next meetings
- Kickoff: Tue, May 10, 10:00 AM PT — 30m (Ben/Marissa/Vivek + Alex/Jordan) — I'll send a calendar invite.
- Tech sync (integration): Wed, May 12, 11:00 AM PT — deep dive for Jordan and infra.

I'll attach the SOW and infra diagram here so your procurement team can start reviewing.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: redwood-sow-draft-v1.pdf; redwood-infra-diagram.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medgrowth.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — MedGrowth: technical fit & PoC plan

Quick technical notes from CS/implementation perspective — Alex, Jordan: adding these so Jordan can triage before our Wed tech sync.

1) SDKs & runtime
- Python SDK: shades of installation — pip package 'redwood' supports sync/async and includes a small local replay harness.
- Node SDK: available for quick ingestion tests; not required for core triage service.

2) Config & compatibility
- API: OpenAI-compatible REST (completion/chat/embeddings) with identical request/response shapes; additional headers for trace_id and client_region.
- Sequence length: we recommend a 1024-token cap for triage summaries to balance cost and quality; PoC can test 512 vs 1024.

3) Telemetry & ops handoff
- We'll add a per-route dashboard for your team in Redwood Console and grant Jordan read-only access for the PoC window.
- We'll also provide a short runbook for failover (fallback to a smaller model variant) — good to validate at load.

If you want, Vivek and I can run a 30-minute onboarding walkthrough the day after kickoff to walk your devs through the SDK and sample integration.

See you on May 10.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0202
